A `.nvsr` request file can name a mount: `--MOUNT--`, the prefix on its first line and
one glob capture per line after it (`crates/nvs-test/src/request.rs`'s module doc).
`nvs run --request` carries it to the carrier the way `nvs_server::mount::carry` does,
so `/` reads as `""`. A prefix no mount table could hold and a blank capture line are
refused.

`Core\Request::jsonAs`, `method` and `mount` owe nothing. `mount` has `about.md`, three
examples, an attack (`tests/hostile/core/Request/mount/`, a capture past the last one and
then every mount kept until the memory limit), a bench (6 allocations per read: the
instance, its array and the strings), and its Rust test carries `covers:`.

`dossier-core-request-2-2` still fails on seven members: `path`, `query`, `queryAs`,
`post`, `postAs`, `scheme` and `route`. Each owes examples, an attack and a bench, and
most owe a `covers:` marker on a Rust test.

items.text: **`Core\Request::scheme`** — owes examples, hostile, perf and a `covers:` marker (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). The Rust test is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:4423` and the member `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:2511`. `--SCHEME--` in the `.nvsr` sets it.

**`Core\Request::path`** — owes examples, hostile, perf and a `covers:` marker (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). The member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:2109`; a `--MOUNT--` beside `--PATH--` shows the stripped path.
**`Core\Request::query`** — the same four; the member is `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/request.rs:2121`.

backlog: `queryAs`, `post`, `postAs`, `route` — the same proofs, after the group above (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`).

A `.nvsr` accepts any non-blank capture; a server only produces `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` (`rule:http-server/a-mount-table-expands-at-boot`). Tightening the reader is optional — `crates/nvs-test/src/request.rs`.
An array index past the end throws `RuntimeError`; whether a narrower class belongs there is not checked — owner: the array module doc.
